Zambian Copper Output Rebounds as Workers End Strike

Copper production in Zambia is returning to normal after a week-long strike by workers in the Metals & Mining industry was resolved late last week, industry officials confirmed. The walkout, which began on June 12 and involved over 4,500 workers across the Copperbelt region, led to significant disruptions at major facilities, including Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd.

The strike was triggered by demands for improved wages and safer working conditions. Negotiations between union representatives and company management intensified as the stoppage continued to affect output. According to the Zambia Mineworkers Union, daily copper processing volumes fell by up to 30% at some sites during the industrial action.

“Operations at Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd and several other plants were severely constrained,” said John Mwape, a union spokesperson. “Our members were committed to ensuring their voices were heard regarding fair compensation and workplace safety.”

Industry analysts estimate that Zambia, Africa’s second-largest copper producer, saw a reduction of approximately 7,000 metric tons in copper output during the seven-day disruption. The immediate impact on export schedules and local supply chains was evident, with some shipments delayed as plants slowed or temporarily halted smelting operations.

The dispute was resolved following a marathon 18-hour negotiation session mediated by the Ministry of Labour. The agreement includes a phased wage increase of 12% over the next 18 months and a commitment to enhanced safety protocols, union leaders said. Management at affected companies, including Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd and Redridge Mining Corp., have confirmed that operations have fully resumed.

“We are pleased to have reached an amicable solution and are committed to working closely with our employees moving forward,” said a Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd spokesperson in a statement. The Zambia Chamber of Mines welcomed the outcome, noting that stable industrial relations are crucial to maintaining the sector’s competitiveness.

As production resumes, industry observers will be watching closely to assess whether the new agreement leads to improved morale and sustained output in Zambia’s vital copper sector.
